summary.value: The Hrvatica is a Croatian farm chicken. It was bred in 1917 by Ivan Lakus at Torcec, a Podravina village, starting from local hens and crossing them with Leghorn cocks. White birds were culled, leaving black, red, brown and speckled birds, and Welsummer blood later set the final type. Today it is kept across Croatia and much of the Balkans. It is a solid dual purpose bird: cocks weigh about 7.5 to 9 pounds and hens about 5.5 to 6.5 pounds. With good feed and care, hens can lay more than 200 eggs a year. The meat is well regarded, especially from birds with access to green feed. Hens still go broody readily and are careful mothers, which is now rare in chickens. The breed resists disease and breeds well, making it a practical choice for small farms that want to hatch their own chicks.
